exact_statement: For every finite nonnegative real length simplex and real value/row exponents, the first_endpoint_universal and second_endpoint_universal inequality systems listed in report.md are inconsistent.

hypotheses.common: Finite I, a_i>=0, sum a_i=1, real v_i and r; zero lengths and negative values allowed
hypotheses.first: Unsaved lower bound; all natural multiplicity cubic bounds on weighted lengths in [1/2,2]; single-factor Gram bounds on [7/5,19/10]; conditional full-factor upper bound at a_i=1
hypotheses.second: v_i<=a_i; unsaved lower bound; r<=2/3; r+4*sum v_i<=4; every positive factor's repeated ordinary bound; conditional full-factor upper bound at a_i=1

decisive_argument: Raising and omitting factors forces all first-endpoint defects to zero and r=2/3, contradicting the Gram gap; scalar forcing and a high-value repeated factor contradict r=2/3 at the second endpoint. Numeric full-factor bounds remove length one.
attribution: Existing Argus exponent argument, not a new result claimed by this review
